sentences.text: 1  JUDGMENT Amit Rawal, J.
The present appeal is at the instance of the landowner whose land measuring 0.4880 hectares has been acquired vide notification caused under Section 4 of the erstwhile Act on 17.12.2009.
Award was passed on 16.9.2010 fixing the rate per hectare as Rs.21,16,117/-.

Dissatisfied with the same,
reference was preferred ie., LAR No.10 of 2010 which relates to properties having an extent of 0.0496 hectare, 0.1203 hectare and 0.3361 hectares.
The acquired properties are situated on the side of Tippu Sulthan road which is very busy and in a locality having much commercial importance.
There is a facility of Roru boat service from Koottayi Azhimukham to Ponnani.
The tourist centre of the Koottayi Azhimukham Tourism Programme is situated near the acquired properties.
There are schools, Teachers Training Institute, B.Ed college, Hospital and place of worships very near to the acquired properties.
The acquired properties would have fetched at least Rs.75,000/- per cent at the time of acquisition ie., 1,85,25,000/-.
The properties have got road frontage throughout having vehicular access.
The land acquisition officer ought not to have reduced the value by applying the anology of portion lying in a lower level or away from the road.

In fact the distance of the sale deeds Exts.A1, A2 and A3 placed on record is of 100, 150 and 125 ms respectively from the LA.APP. NO.
157 OF 2013 basic land and the rate of the aforementioned land was much higher than the one assessed.

Appellant before the Tribunal besides rendering the testimony as AW1 brought on record Exts.A1 to A4, the details of which are given hereunder:
A1 - Certified copy of document No.3359/2009 of SRO, Kodakkal A2 - Certified copy of document No.31200/2009 of SRO, Kodakkal A3 - Certified copy of document No.3536/2009 of SRO, Kodakkal A4 - Letter of Executive Engineer, Kerala State Housing Board, Malappuram Division, Malappuram dated 6.12011 2.

entities.text: Kerala State Housing Board, Malappuram Division
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Whereas the respondent placed on record B1 certified copy of Document No.3535/2009 of SRO, Kodakkal.
Commission report and sketch are Exts. C1 to C2(a).
It is pertinent to mention here that the first report of the Commissioner were discarded by the Tribunal and was remitted for conducting the inspection afresh.
The fresh inspection report is Ext.C2 and the sketch is Ext. C2(a).

Learned Tribunal though noticed that the value of the sale deed Ext.A1, A2 and A3 is Rs.23,000/-, 22,000/-
and 24,000/- per cent but assessed the compensation of the three blocks as 18,886/-, 14,680/- and 12,584/-, and per cent respectively.
3. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant submitted that the land acquisition Tribunal has undertaken the exercise of belting system by taking into consideration the rate of the land.
Though there was a 30% reduction for the area being used as burial by the land acquisition collector but has been reduced to LA.APP. NO. 157 OF 2013 10% against 30% of reduction.

No plausible and reasonable explanation has come forward in ignoring the price of the sale deed Exts.A1, A2 and A3 which are of three notifications dated 24.8.2009, 25.8.2009 and 8.9.2009 whereas the notice of K.P.O.Rahmathulla vs The Special Tahsildar La(Gen.) on 8 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27804062/
2 acquisition was of 17.12.2009.

entities.text: K.P.O.Rahmathulla vs The Special Tahsildar La(Gen.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The reason for discarding was that the distance of Exts.A1, A2 and A3 to be farther from the basic land which has been taken as basis for purpose of assessing the compensation considering it to be immediately adjacent to the acquired land.
The Tribunal has failed to notice the sketch Ext.C2 which shows that the lands in Exts.A1, A2 and A3 are also adjacent to the acquired land having a common road viz-a-viz basic land.

4. On the other hand, learned Government Pleader supported the aforementioned findings and submitted that the reasoning assigned by the Land Acquisition Tribunal / Sub court is perfectly legal and justified for the reason that it is based upon the belting system as part of the land was being used for burial and therefore reduction of 10% is justified.
The location/ distance of the lands Exts.A1, A2 and A3 are farther than the basic land ie., 100, 150 and 175 ms respectively.
5. We have heard the learned counsel for the parties and appraised the paper book.
The facts as noticed above, with regard to the date of acquisition, assessment of compensation by the Land Acquisition Collector are not in dispute.

The factors which are LA.APP. NO. 157 OF 2013 required to be taken into consideration for the purpose of determining the enhancement or reduction sought by either of the parties to the lis are as under:
1) location only, without, belting system 2) The sale deeds prior to the notification caused under Section 4 of the Act 3) The distance of the basic land whether situated close to the road / horizontally.
4) The location of the property referred to in Exts.A1, A2 and A3 executed concededly before the date of the publication of the notification under Section 4 of the Act.
6. As per the site plan Ext.C2(a) properties referred in Ext.A1, A2 and A3, are adjacent to each other having a common access/road (vertically) and not horizontally.
Thus the value of the land situated farther to the basic land cannot be said to be less by believing that it does not have access.

No doubt,
the Tribunal/sub court has taken the reduction of the land being lower in the area, in and around the burial ground and being sloppy as 10% but the fact remains the purpose for which the land required has totally been ignored.
The land has been acquired by the Government for rehabilitating the tsunami victims ie., to provide small quarters/place of residence for them.

This has to be equally distributed and thus there would not be any marginal difference between the price LA.APP. NO. 157 OF 2013 depending upon the fact that all the houses would have a different access.
At the best, the houses which were closer to the sea/ocean would have a risk of tsunami, may fetch a lesser price.

We draw our support from the ratio of decidendi culled out in the judgment in Patiala urban Planning and Development Authority v. Tarlochan Singh (2020 (17) SCC 224), Bijender and Others v. State of Haryana & Others (2017 AIR SC 5811) and Ashrafi vs. State of Haryana (2013 (5) SCC 527.
7.

sentences.text:
For the reason aforementioned, we are of the view that the reasoning assigned by the land acquisition Tribunal/sub Court in not granting the compensation as mentioned in Exts.A1, A2 and A3 by emphatically relying upon the price of the land referred to in Ext.B1, basic land, is wholly K.P.O.Rahmathulla vs The Special Tahsildar La(Gen.) on 8 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27804062/
3 erroneous and illegal.

entities.text: K.P.O.Rahmathulla vs The Special Tahsildar La(Gen.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, we modify the award of the Land Acquisition Tribunal/sub Court and enhanced the compensation by taking Rs.24,000/- as mentioned in Ext.A3 (247 cents x 24,000/-) ie., 59,28,000/- per hectare.
The appellants shall also be entitled to all the statutory benefits which are permissible under the erstwhile land acquisition Act.
